knownGaps: Focused S3/PostgreSQL, multipart, checksum, governed deduplication, consent, privacy-maintenance, semantic-redaction, job restart, stream reconnect/backpressure, provider, transport, and black-box verification is deferred.
Production profile remains prohibited until durable artifact/job/stream/consent state, privacy erasure, remote providers, recovery, failure injection, and canonical evidence pass.

ai-inference.activationCondition: selected Media provider delegates generic model inference

requirements.statement: Media exposes a standalone tenant-scoped consent, artifact, asynchronous processing-job, reconnectable streaming, and privacy-maintenance runtime over typed stores and providers.
requirements.rationale: A large provider module graph requires one stable lifecycle and transport boundary instead of a health-only launcher.
requirements.scope: Media runtime contracts, launcher, consent lifecycle, artifact lifecycle, jobs, stream sessions, privacy maintenance, providers, transport, and shutdown
nonGoals: Persisting media blobs in Data Cloud
preconditions: Exactly one artifact, job, and stream store plus at least one processing and streaming provider are ready; external providers additionally require durable consent authority
requirements.successBehavior: Consent is tenant/principal bound, uploads resume sequentially and complete only after size/hash verification, jobs execute asynchronously with governed results, streams reconnect with leases and ordered bounded buffers, and expired durable media state is physically purged.
requirements.failureBehavior: Invalid/revoked consent, out-of-order chunks/frames, checksum mismatch, missing providers, invalid tokens, expired leases, concurrency exhaustion, backpressure, timeout, cancellation, or unsafe de-identification remain explicit and fail closed.
requirements.securityInvariant: All consent/artifact/job/stream routes are authenticated and tenant scoped; raw credentials, location/device metadata, raw biometric vectors, and raw media fields are not persisted in runtime metadata/results; external processing requires authority-owned consent and residency grants.
requirements.reliabilityInvariant: Consent state, job terminal states, artifact references, upload finalization claims, and stream sessions are durable before exposure; erasure removes object bytes before metadata truth is deleted.
requirements.performanceConstraint: Bodies, chunks, frames, jobs, concurrency, provider attempts, timeouts, multipart parts, buffers, privacy purge batches, and list limits are bounded.

requirements.statement: Artifact ingestion is resumable, sequential, size-bound, checksum-verified, classified, retention-bound, governed-deduplicated, metadata-minimized, and finalized through a durable claim into encrypted object storage.
requirements.rationale: Large privacy-sensitive media cannot rely on unbounded one-shot uploads, unverified object references, or byte-level reuse that weakens metadata policy.
requirements.scope: Upload request/session/chunks/completion, S3 multipart finalization, governed byte deduplication, metadata minimization, and artifact metadata
nonGoals: Serving raw artifact bytes through metadata routes
preconditions: Expected size, SHA-256, file name, content type, classification, retention, and minimized metadata are declared
requirements.successBehavior: Each chunk advances exactly one index and completion publishes immutable encrypted object metadata after full-content SHA-256 validation; same-tenant byte identity reuses an artifact only when file name, content type, classification, metadata, and remaining retention are compatible.
requirements.failureBehavior: Expired, oversized, out-of-order, incomplete, checksum-mismatched, concurrent, stale-finalization, or governed-metadata-incompatible uploads fail closed or recover through the durable claim.
requirements.securityInvariant: Object keys are tenant-opaque, file names are normalized, location/device/credential metadata is removed before persistence, storage paths cannot escape configured roots, and byte equality never lowers classification, metadata, or retention requirements.
requirements.reliabilityInvariant: Artifact metadata references an immutable completed object; stale finalization claims are detectable and recoverable; deduplication is serialized against the tenant-scoped artifact row and returns only policy-compatible state.
requirements.performanceConstraint: Chunk, total size, digest reads, multipart part size/count, provider waits, and deduplication lookup are bounded.

requirements.statement: Media stream sessions are durable, tenant-scoped, consent-governed, token-protected, lease-bound, reconnectable, sequence-ordered, backpressure-aware, and explicitly terminal.
requirements.rationale: Audio/video streaming needs restart-safe session and privacy truth rather than process-local connection state.
requirements.scope: Stream session contracts, PostgreSQL store, consent verification, remote streaming provider, and HTTP lifecycle
preconditions: Stream store and a capability-compatible provider are ready; external streaming additionally has a verified consent decision
requirements.successBehavior: Open verifies consent and returns one connection token, connect renews a bounded lease and re-verifies current consent, frames advance contiguous sequence numbers with live consent, and close can terminate using last verified non-secret consent evidence after revocation.
requirements.failureBehavior: Invalid/revoked consent, invalid tokens, stale versions, expired leases, out-of-order frames, oversized frames, unsupported kinds, provider backpressure, or close failures remain explicit.
requirements.securityInvariant: Only token hashes and non-secret consent evidence are persisted; connection tokens remain header-only and tenant/principal identity is preserved.
requirements.reliabilityInvariant: Reconnect count, last sequence, provider-buffer state, lease expiry, consent identity/provenance, and terminal state survive process restart.
requirements.performanceConstraint: Frame size, buffer capacity, provider calls, lease duration, and active stream counts are bounded.

requirements.statement: Media privacy is enforced through durable consent administration/verification, authority-owned purpose/residency/egress/biometric grants, physical retention and erasure, structural metadata/result minimization, and fail-closed semantic de-identification promotion.
requirements.rationale: Recordings, transcripts, faces, voices, and derived biometric data require executable privacy controls rather than documentation-only claims.
requirements.scope: Consent grant/revoke/verification, privacy maintenance, metadata/result sanitization, external provider governance, semantic transcript promotion, health, routes, and shutdown
nonGoals: Treating structural key filtering as semantic transcript de-identification
Enabling an anonymous transcript tier without semantic-redaction evidence
preconditions: Production has durable consent and privacy-maintenance providers; de-identified promotion additionally has a ready semantic-redaction provider
requirements.successBehavior: External media is dispatched only under matching active authority grants; revoked consent blocks new processing while existing sessions remain terminable; expired object bytes and metadata are physically removed; sensitive fields are minimized; DEIDENTIFIED promotion requires provider-owned positive classification and provenance.
requirements.failureBehavior: Missing/revoked consent, disallowed purpose/region/egress/biometrics, erasure failure, unavailable redactor, redactor identity mismatch, unsafe classification, or redaction timeout fail closed without persisting raw sensitive output as a promoted result.
requirements.securityInvariant: Callers cannot self-authorize consent permissions or de-identification; credential/raw-biometric/raw-media fields are excluded from durable job results and semantic-redaction provenance is structurally sanitized.
requirements.reliabilityInvariant: Consent and retention truth are durable and revocation-aware; purge failures keep metadata for retry; semantic-redaction failures produce terminal failure state without promoted raw content.
requirements.performanceConstraint: Consent lists, privacy purge cycles, result depth/field counts, redaction timeout, and provider fan-out are bounded.

requirements.statement: Media exposes canonical, modality-grounded STT, TTS, vision, and multimodal provider contracts with explicit provider identity, health/degradation truth, bounded execution, and consent/privacy enforcement.
requirements.rationale: Typed modality boundaries prevent generic text-completion output from masquerading as speech or visual inference and make provider failure observable and fail-closed.
requirements.scope: Media modality capability discovery, provider health, degradation policy, execution bounds, typed result shape, provenance, consent, privacy, and multimodal context
nonGoals: Using generic text completion as an STT, TTS, vision, or multimodal substitute
Reintroducing a remote Vision adapter outside the typed provider boundary
preconditions: A provider declares the modality it serves, provider/model identity, processing boundary, health/degradation posture, and bounded execution limits
requirements.successBehavior: STT, TTS, vision, and multimodal results carry an explicit modality and grounded payload shape plus provider/model provenance; external execution requires active authority-owned consent and privacy-compatible residency/retention; provider absence is reported as unavailable/degraded truth rather than a fabricated successful result.
requirements.failureBehavior: Mismatched modality payloads, generic text-completion masquerading, oversized/deep results, missing provider identity, unavailable providers, expired or mismatched consent, disallowed residency/retention, or biometric output without eligibility fail closed.
requirements.securityInvariant: Raw media, credentials, biometric vectors, and ungoverned multimodal context do not cross or enter the durable result boundary; consent permissions remain authority-owned and cannot be widened by callers.
requirements.reliabilityInvariant: Provider identity, health, degradation policy, bounded execution, and terminal failure truth remain explicit across capability discovery and job completion.
requirements.performanceConstraint: Modality input/output, result fields/depth, collections, provider waits, and execution concurrency remain bounded.
